standard.title: Reflect on dance works to inform practice
standard.description: reflect on own and others' dance works and/or practices to inform choreographic choices and use of technical and expressive skills
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use teacher feedback to reflect on own dance practice (AC9ADA6D02). They have not yet systematically investigated others' dance works as a source of influence, or used reflection to document and direct practice development over time.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students reflect on own and others' dance works to make and document informed choices about choreography and technical/expressive skill use.

nodes.label: Investigating others' dance works as influence
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how other dancers' and choreographers' use of elements, devices and techniques influences own practice choices
nodes.minimum_width: Investigate at least one example of how another dancer or choreographer uses an element of dance or style-specific technique; explain how this informs a specific choice in own practice
nodes.typical_width: Document a range of examples of how others use elements of dance or style-specific techniques in a journal; explain how each example informs choices in own choreography or performance
wider: Develop a personal archive of influences — journal entries documenting how specific examples of others' work open new directions in own practice

Investigate how two choreographers with contrasting approaches to the same element of dance make different expressive choices — analyse what each reveals and use the comparison to sharpen own approach
Research a choreographer whose work has directly influenced a dance style and trace the chain of influence into contemporary practice

response_modes.reason: Students need to build a personal repertoire of influences — documented examples of how others use elements and techniques — before reflection on influences can become a genuine practice habit. A single example is insufficient; accumulated references build the vocabulary for informed choreographic decision-making.

success_criteria: Investigates at least one example of another artist's use of an element or technique
Explains how the example informs a specific choice in own practice
Does not reduce influence to 'inspiration' — connects specific observation to specific decision

nodes.label: Using feedback to refine dance
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use feedback from peers, self-observation and teachers to identify specific refinements to choreography and technical/expressive skills
nodes.minimum_width: Respond to at least one piece of feedback with a documented change in choreography or skill use; explain what the feedback revealed and what changed
nodes.typical_width: Use feedback from peers who have observed a workshop or rehearsal to identify refinements; document how feedback leads to specific changes in dance; evaluate outcomes
wider: Use video self-review alongside peer feedback — compare what each reveals and evaluate how video feedback identifies things that peer observation misses
Develop criteria for evaluating own rehearsal footage — go beyond 'it looked good/bad' to articulate specific technical and expressive standards
Evaluate how different feedback sources (self, peer, teacher) reveal different aspects of dance — develop a personal feedback integration strategy

response_modes.reason: Using feedback productively — receiving it, interpreting it against dance criteria, and translating it into changed practice — is a reflective habit that develops through repeated cycles. Students need sustained practice with the feedback loop, not exposure to more feedback contexts.

success_criteria: Responds to at least one piece of feedback with a documented change
Explains what the feedback revealed and what changed as a result
Change is specific — not a vague 'I improved'

nodes.label: Sustained reflection on practice development
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use sustained reflection on own and others' dance to show how practice has developed over time and where it is heading
nodes.minimum_width: Show at least one example where reflection led to a changed practice direction over time; explain what changed and what the reflection revealed
nodes.typical_width: Document how practice has developed across a unit as a result of sustained reflection on own and others' dance; evaluate how movement vocabulary and technical/expressive range have grown
wider: Reflect on how movement vocabulary has extended across a unit — identify specific moments where encountering others' work opened new directions
Develop a personal artistic statement articulating the influences currently shaping own dance practice and how they are being engaged and adapted
Evaluate own choreographic or performance development against specific criteria — identify what has developed, what remains a goal, and what new directions have emerged

response_modes.reason: This node integrates influence investigation (Node 1) and feedback cycles (Node 2) into a sustained account of practice development. Students who can reflect on single moments but cannot demonstrate development over time have not met the descriptor's demand for reflection that informs ongoing practice.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The personal artistic statement direction gives advancing students a genuine opportunity to synthesise reflection into an articulated practice identity — thinking about themselves as developing artists with a perspective and direction, not just as students completing tasks.
success_criteria: Shows at least one example where reflection led to changed practice direction over time
Documentation demonstrates development — not just a single reflection moment
Reflection on others' work and own feedback is connected to increasingly informed practice choices
